title: Close the Loop: Profile Feedback
subtitle: Turn the archive into a catalog improvement
scenario: It is the start date, 9:00 AM. The archived run holds a small lesson: on day one, the Logistics Coordinator needed a handheld scanner that the role profile never listed. Turn that observation into a proposed catalog change and route it to the owner. This is how the workflow gets smarter each run.
input: Archive note for hire H-4021 (Logistics Coordinator): on day one the hire needed a handheld scanner to do the job, but the role profile did not list it (inProfile = false). Propose adding it to the catalog and route the change to the People Ops Lead, who owns the catalog.
instructions: Record the role and what the hire needed.
Note whether it was already in the profile (inProfile).
Set the proposed change (add) and route it to the catalog owner.
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON profile-feedback record: role, needed, inProfile (boolean), proposedChange, and routedTo. The hire needed a handheld scanner not in the profile, so inProfile is false, proposedChange is add, routed to the People Ops Lead.
successMessage: Loop closed. The catalog owner has a concrete, governed proposal from what this run actually taught.
editorHelper: Propose the change - the owner ratifies it, you do not rewrite the catalog.

intro.heading: The loop close: teach the catalog

sections.title: Every run is a lesson
sections.body: The archive is not just for audit. It holds what the role actually needed versus what the profile listed. Feeding that back is how the catalog stops being a guess and becomes evidence-based.

sections.title: Propose, do not rewrite
sections.body: Feedback routes a proposed change to the People Ops Lead, who owns the catalog. It does not silently edit the matrix - governance still decides. The loop informs; the owner ratifies.

sections.title: Concrete beats vague
sections.body: 'The profile was incomplete' helps no one. 'Add a handheld scanner for Logistics Coordinator' is a change someone can approve. Specific feedback is what actually improves the next hire.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A profile-feedback record that closes the temporal loop into the role profile catalog - the same catalog the next hire's plan will expand.

fieldGuide.meaning: The role the feedback is about.
fieldGuide.hint: The role from the archive: Logistics Coordinator.

fieldGuide.meaning: What the hire actually needed on day one.
fieldGuide.hint: The item the profile did not list: a handheld scanner.

fieldGuide.meaning: Whether it was already in the role profile.
fieldGuide.hint: It was not listed, so the boolean false.

fieldGuide.meaning: The change proposed to the catalog.
fieldGuide.hint: Propose to add the missing item.

fieldGuide.meaning: The catalog owner who ratifies the change.
fieldGuide.hint: The People Ops Lead owns the catalog.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd jot 'this role also needs a scanner' after onboarding and send it to whoever owns the role checklist to update.

bestFit.how: create a catalog change-request record assigned to People Ops when a run needed something off-profile
diff what was actually granted against the profile and file the delta as a change request

takeaway.heading: Loop closed
points: You turned an archive observation into a concrete catalog proposal.
The change is routed to the People Ops Lead - proposed, not silently applied.
Specific feedback (add a handheld scanner) is something an owner can act on.
The feedback closes the temporal loop back into the role profile catalog.
The workflow can now improve the catalog from what each run actually taught.
